newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada and Chile reach free trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada and Chile reach free trade deal.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday that Canada and Chile reached a free trade agreement, which will be signed during a visit to Ottawa by Chilean President Eduardo Frei this weekend.
"This is a solid deal for both nations and will boost Canadian exports and create jobs in both countries," Eggleton said in a statement.
The agreement, which will become effective on June 2, 1997, includes two parallel deals on environmental and labor cooperation, modelled after the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
The free trade agreement, reached after months of negotiations, provides for immediate duty-free access for most industrial goods, accounting for 80 percent of Canadian exports to Chile.
Under the deal, Chile will scrap its 11 percent import duty on almost all remaining industrial and resource-based goods over five years.
The free trade agreement also provides for better access of Canadian agricultural goods, including durum wheat, barley, lentils, seed potatoes, pork, canola products and beef.

"Canadian exporters' access to Chilean markets will now be better than that of their competitors in the United States, the European Union, Argentina and Brazil," an International Trade Department news release said.
The statement did not say whether Canadian investors would get an exemption of a rule requiring foreigners to deposit 30 percent of their reserves with Chile's central bank.

But it did say, that the agreement contained a provision to automatically grant Canadian investors the "benefits of any further liberalizations that may occur in the future," thus indicating that probably Canada failed to get an exemption to the 30 percent rule.

Under the free trade agreement the two countries will set up a Free Trade Commission and secretariat which will deal with the resolution of any trade disputes that might arise between Ottawa and Santiago.
Under the agreement, the two countries will also eliminate any anti-dumping duties they currently impose within six years.
Minutes after the free trade deal was announced in a Trade Department press release, International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said last-minute "hiccups" had prevented the deal from being finalized.
He said he hoped a final agreement could be reached within hours.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
